about: A condition the general manager attaches when approving an order that takes a customer past their credit limit. The GM types the terms and a deadline at the moment of approval; the rep who raised the order owes them; only the GM closes them. Both apps show and move these, so both implement this file and both test suites read it.
why: Built 22 August 2026 for the phone, extended to the dashboard 7 September 2026. Before it, the GM's terms - clear the sixty-day outstanding by the fifteenth, collect a cheque before the next delivery - lived in a phone call. The approval went through and nobody was accountable for the terms afterwards.

rules.who_sets_it: The GM alone, at the moment of approving. Never the sales manager. A condition recorded later is one somebody has to remember to record. Since 24 Sep 2026 the WORDS usually come from the rep: they write the customer's commitment when raising an over-limit order, and it is what the GM's condition starts as - but it only becomes a condition when the GM approves. See credit_commitment.json.
rules.optional: An approval may carry no condition at all - unless the order carries the rep's commitment, in which case approving always makes one (credit_commitment.json). Without a commitment, plenty do not, and forcing one produces a field full of 'n/a'.
rules.who_answers: The rep who raised the order. Answering moves it Open -> Awaiting Review. It never closes it.
rules.who_closes: The GM alone. The person under an obligation declaring it satisfied is not accountability. Enforced in code on both sides, because this site has no Server Script behind the screen.
rules.send_back: The GM may return it: Awaiting Review -> Open, and the rep's response stays on the record rather than being cleared.
rules.overdue: Past its due date AND not Closed. A condition closed late is not overdue - it is closed. Overdue is what is still owed today, not a history of lateness.
rules.blocks_nothing: No order is ever refused because a condition is open or overdue. A rule that stopped a rep selling in front of a customer over an obligation somebody forgot to close would cost more than it saved.
rules.no_deadline: A condition with no due date is never overdue. It is still owed, and it still shows, but nothing about it is late.

transitions.why: the rep answers an open condition
the GM accepts the answer and closes it
the GM is not satisfied and sends it back, and the answer is kept
the GM may close one the rep never answered - chasing a reply on something already settled helps nobody
a rep cannot close their own obligation, and this is the case the whole rule exists for
a rep cannot close one directly either
a sales manager is not the GM, however senior they feel
answering an already-closed condition changes nothing
the GM may reopen a closed condition if it turns out it was not met
answering twice before review just replaces the answer

overdue.why: due today is not yet late
awaiting the GM's review and past its date is still owed
closed late is closed, not overdue
an unset date read back as the string null is not a deadline either
